sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Pelatro has a credible software growth proposition, but its operating-cash presentation and acquisition bridge are not yet reliable enough for an ordinary investment rating. Classification: research hold, with a speculative growth watchlist rather than a confirmed compounder designation. This is not a short recommendation or a finding of fraud.

The positive case is substantial. FY26 CVM revenue rose 35.91% without counting Estel's acquired revenue, and the next quarter's core growth was 25.11%. Internal product development is expensed, a favorable feature often missed when all software intangibles are called capitalized R&D. Telecom integrations and cross-selling can produce useful operating leverage. At the verified ₹393 reference price, reported TTM P/E is 20.85 x rather than an obviously prohibitive multiple.

The obstacle is the distinction between profit, growth and money available to owners. Receivables plus unbilled assets grew about 142.7%, to ₹48.21 cr, against 61.2% reported sales growth. Prepayments also expanded sharply. The published cash-flow statements contain borrowing, acquired-liability and noncash lease/goodwill movements that prevent a clean normalized conversion measure. Existing audits are unmodified, but that does not make every operating-cash classification suitable for valuation.

BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, without neutral imputation. Individual strengths and weaknesses are scored where evidence supports them. A base case excluding deposits needs additional accessible cash or collections to maintain the analyst's reserve; using all published deposits keeps it funded. Therefore G3 is Conditional, not an actual-distress finding. Until the G2 reconciliation is resolved, attractive conditional model returns must not be promoted as an expected return or executable buy price.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Factor scores are GOV 5, MOAT 6, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R NS, D 4, P NS and L NS. Confidence, evidence, source identifiers, reasons and re-scoring requirements accompany every factor. No unobserved factor is assigned a neutral 5. Medium-confidence evidence does not support a score above 8.

BQS weights are GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. The known weighted contribution is 4.94, with 88% coverage and an uncapped missing-factor range of 5.06–6.14. GQS uses REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH 10%; its known contribution is 5.60, coverage 85%, and uncapped diagnostic range 5.75–7.10. Persistent weak cash realization triggers the growth-quality maximum of 5. The uncapped range and policy ceiling are displayed separately; neither turns missing CAP into a point score.

IAS uses unrounded BQS25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10%. Only D contributes 0.80, so coverage is 20% and its mathematical missing-data range is 1.60–8.80. These are mathematical bounds from unknown factors, not confidence intervals or investable ratings. The cap is a methodology choice, not an empirical forecast of returns.

All three points remain NS and all three ranking-eligibility flags are false. There is no hidden composite ranking, no rounded BQS fed into IAS, and no promotion to a quality-growth category based on the upper end of an uncertainty range. The selected REV window is the explicit two-year exception, because a superior three/five-year group organic series does not exist; the quarter does not add an extra point.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The listed Indian company was incorporated in March 2013, first as Kivar Infotech, later Pelatro Solutions, and became a public company in 2024. It is not interchangeable with the former UK-listed Pelatro parent or every entity using that brand. The Indian company acquired Singapore in January 2024, then added Estel's Indian software business and an overseas subsidiary in July 2025. Group economics, shareholder rights and historical growth must follow this legal perimeter.

The core CVM suite helps telecommunications operators target campaigns, manage loyalty and leads, analyze consumer behavior and execute communications. Estel adds recharge, vouchers, distribution and mobile-financial-service products. Management reports 46 operator networks in 33 countries, approximately 1.5 billion consumers served and 490 employees. These are company operating statistics, not independent proof of paying users, market share or network effects; some presentations use a different country count.

The business combines recurring commitments, repeat change requests and one-time work. FY26 mix was 60% recurring,22% reoccurring and 18% one-time, versus 67/20/13 in FY25. Repeat change requests are economically useful but are not a committed subscription ARR balance. Statutory revenue is classified as sale of services and does not provide an audited split between perpetual licenses, term licenses, subscriptions, implementation and managed services. It would be wrong to apply a pure SaaS valuation simply because the product is software.

The cost base is principally people, implementation, hosting/operations, product development and customer support. Product engineering is expensed under the consolidated policy. Purchased IP is a separate balance-sheet item, and acquisitions add goodwill. Thus the company can be physically asset-light while remaining cash-hungry if recognition precedes invoicing or operator payment. The useful unit of analysis is collected, recurring profit after product upkeep and implementation effort, not licenses or platform users alone.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
An operator does not replace a deployed campaign/data platform as casually as an ordinary office application. Integrations, historical models, security reviews, workflow changes and trained teams create switching friction. Management describes roughly 10–12 months of sales effort and 6–8 months of implementation in some situations. An installed customer base can lower the cost of selling adjacent products, and the acquisition joins CVM with recharge/distribution tools used in related operator processes.

These features support MOAT 6, not a proven exceptional franchise. The same long deployment cycle delays revenue and cash and can increase customer bargaining power. A small population of large operators can internalize applications or select a broad competing suite. Amdocs' own FY25 disclosures show a large managed-services component in a much broader operator platform; Subex is another telecom software/data context. Neither is a like-for-like pure SaaS multiple to be copied, and no contemporary peer trading multiple is used to manufacture a fair value.

The IPO concentration data showed the largest customer at 18.38% of FY24 revenue, top three 31.97%, top five 39.09% and top ten 48.70%. These dated figures are not carried forward as current facts after the perimeter changes. FY26 customer concentration, cohort renewal, gross retention, net retention, churn, deployment-level profitability and contractual price escalation are not sufficiently disclosed to quantify pricing power. Over 90% of FY26 revenue is outside India, exposing the company to varied currencies, payment practices and approvals.

Management's approximately₹12,000 cr market opportunity and 450-operator universe are useful prospecting context, not a verified accessible-revenue denominator. AI could improve campaign results and engineering efficiency, but it can also commoditize tooling and strengthen large-platform competitors. A moat upgrade would require paid retention and price realization without persistent working-capital deterioration.

A third economic comparator is Tecnotree, whose telecom BSS and customer-lifecycle platforms overlap adjacent operator needs. Its FY2025 annual report records capitalized development equal to 13.4% of revenue and a five-year amortization policy, materially unlike Pelatro’s expensed internal development. Amdocs, Subex and Tecnotree therefore form a three-company product/economic comparison, not a synchronized relative-valuation set. Their reported EBITDA margins cannot be copied without accounting and service-mix adjustments.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The headline FY26 revenue increase from₹85.7687 cr to₹138.2301 cr is 61.1661%. It consists of₹30.7999 cr additional CVM revenue and₹21.6615 cr of Estel revenue consolidated for nine months. Core CVM rose from₹85.7687 cr to₹116.5686 cr,35.9104%, the appropriate acquisition-adjusted annual comparison. This is constant acquisition scope, not constant currency; volume, pricing and FX contributions are not separately authenticated.

The FY24 audited group total₹54.9922 cr contains only a partial Singapore period and is unsuitable as the denominator for a clean full-group organic CAGR. A hypothetical full-year FY24 pro forma CVM total₹73.0274 cr provides the explicit two-year exception: growth to FY26₹116.5686 cr is 26.3420% annualized. FY25 versus that hypothetical base is 17.4473%. The pro forma practitioner's work and assumptions are retained as a different assurance category from audited actuals.

Earlier standalone revenue was₹40.7547 cr in FY22, ₹48.9823 cr in FY23 and₹58.8082 cr in FY24, with FY21 original-GAAP revenue₹33.0569 cr as additional context. That India delivery business and later consolidated customer-revenue business are not the same perimeter. Three-, five- and ten-year comparable group organic growth are therefore ND, not zero and not backfilled with a cherry-picked predecessor CAGR.

Q1FY27 group revenue₹40.2198 cr rose 50.6867%; CVM₹33.3926 cr rose 25.1081%, and Estel supplied₹6.8272 cr. This corroborates demand but does not justify annualizing one quarter into certainty or awarding an additional REV point. TTM revenue toJune 2026 is₹151.7589 cr, using FY26 plus Q1FY27 less Q1FY26. Only profit-and-loss fields have that TTM bridge; no unauthenticated TTM CFO is invented. Management says substantial yearly target coverage is in hand, but its statement is not converted into a firm absolute order book without terms and cancellation conditions.

The June 12,2024 practitioner report gives SAE 3420 assurance on compilation, not a fresh audit of the underlying periods or assurance that the hypothetical outcome would actually have occurred. Note 3 retains each entity’s accounting policies without uniformity adjustments. This limits the two-year proxy to Medium confidence; it is not represented as a fully uniform audited growth history.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth can be valuable here without an industrial-scale factory cycle. Internal development is expensed, common platforms can serve additional operators, and cross-selling to existing deployments may require less incremental selling effort than a new customer. The correct question is whether incremental after-tax operating profit exceeds the full capital needed for implementation, customer credit, acquired capabilities and recurring replacement, not whether physical capex is small.

The accounting capital bridges are retained for FY24, FY25, FY26 and June 2026. They start from equity plus debt and leases less gross cash and deferred-tax assets, and remove ROU assets for a cash-rent convention. Goodwill and purchased IP remain visible. Seller creditors and contingent obligations are shown as additional committed-capital screens rather than blindly counting paid acquisition capex twice. These are diagnostic balances, not a credible organic incremental-return series.

FY24 includes a restructuring acquisition at nominal cash consideration with a large negative-net-asset goodwill effect. FY25 introduces acquired IP and a large noncash office lease. FY26 adds Estel, goodwill, acquired working capital and contingent consideration. No matched segment capital/profit bridge isolates organic CVM investment from purchased growth or establishes the maturation lag. CAP is therefore NS, not low merely because the company has goodwill and not high merely because headline ROCE is attractive. A coherent aggregate organic bridge could resolve this without private project-by-project data.

The model retains development in operating margins, uses annual physical/replacement capex and charges a ten-year economic life to purchased IP. It does not add a fictional development asset, subtract amortization twice, or assume all disclosed EBITDA can be distributed. Working capital is tied to billed days, unbilled days, prepayments/other assets and customer/supplier financing. The most immediate reinvestment bottleneck is cash tied up before customer acceptance and payment. Product breadth and market size only become a durable runway when collections and after-dilution returns validate them.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter ownership is 52.62%, with 47.38% public holdings. September 2026 disclosures report 50,000 promoter shares pledged, approximately 0.9% of promoter shares and 0.47% of total issued shares. The earlier unpledged position is not rolled forward. Promoter locked shares total 4,312,390 and public locked shares 429,900, so headline public ownership is not the same as fully available float. Individual shareholder identifiers are not needed for this analysis.

Governance concerns must retain both allegations and dated counterevidence. Former UK shareholders alleged undervalued transfers and missing shareholder consent in an August 2024 letter; the prospectus records counsel rejecting the allegations. No final adverse ruling or final exoneration was found. The 2020 SEBI proceeding concerned disclosure/preclearance breaches in Subex off-market transfers, with a₹2 lakh joint/several penalty. The order did not quantify unfair gain/investor loss or establish repetitive default and recorded mitigating circumstances. IPO disclosures also describe concluded 2022 RBI compounding totaling₹20.72 lakh across eight orders. These are historical compliance findings, not proof of Pelatro accounting fraud.

Recent main audits and control reports are clean. FY24 did disclose a short audit-trail gap and a CSR transfer observation, and FY22 noted old IGST dues. Later reports provide counterevidence rather than allowing those issues to be presented as indefinitely current. The October 2024 auditor resignation letter expressly attributes the proposed replacement to listing and enhanced reporting requirements; it does not report a disagreement. The FY23 original report's responsibilities annexure is not mislabeled as an IFC effectiveness opinion.

Related-party transactions include promoter loans, compensation and expense reimbursements; a large India-to-Singapore demand loan eliminates on consolidation. These require scrutiny and are not automatically diversion. The promoter loan outstanding₹1.5 cr and its scheduled repayments are included within debt, not added again. IPO monitoring shows funds fully used byDecember 2025 following approved object reallocation; there is no untouched IPO cash cushion.

Execution is mixed. Core growth and Estel revenue are real achievements, but lower Q 1 Estel margins and persistent unbilled growth leave the self-funding transition unproven. November 2025 management acknowledged weak free cash and anticipated improvement. Its metric is not formally reconciled to statutory CFO, so the analysis avoids a false exact target-miss calculation while retaining the need for cash-backed milestones.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Reported profitability is improving, but the route from operating profit to distributable cash needs reconstruction. FY26 operating EBITDA excluding other income is₹25.9779 cr, whereas management-style EBITDA including other income is₹31.4755 cr. The₹5.4976 cr difference includes₹4.7396 cr FX gains, ₹0.6517 cr interest and₹0.1063 cr effective-interest adjustments. FX can recur and is not automatically fraudulent or exceptional, but it is not assumed to be a stable operating margin. FY25 other income also included₹2.0215 cr liability write-back.

Purchased IP is₹16.0332 cr atMarch 2026, versus₹14.5399 cr a year earlier; the₹1.4933 cr movement is translation, not newly capitalized internal development. The issuer does not amortize this asset. An analyst ten-year economic-life charge is₹1.6033 cr annually, explicitly a sensitivity rather than a purported audit correction. With cash rent replacing ROU depreciation, normalized FY26 EBIT is₹17.3127 cr and NOPAT at 20% tax₹13.8501 cr. FY25 on the same convention is₹9.4978 cr EBIT and₹7.5982 cr NOPAT. FY26 reported PAT₹18.1048 cr benefits from an effective tax rate around 6.3%; neither that tax rate nor FX gains is mechanically projected forever. The₹1.6778 cr exceptional gratuity-related charge is separately visible.

Comparatives require care. The original FY25 PBT₹15.0255 cr becomes₹13.0908 cr in the later comparative, with the same₹1.9347 cr reduction in current tax and unchanged PAT₹11.8935 cr. Tax-paid presentation moves by the same amount; other income and other expenses also regroup. This is not portrayed as a revised bottom-line profit. An explicit published regrouping explanation is still useful for reliable analytical comparability. Historical original AS statements, later Ind AS restatements and the FY24 pro forma statement remain separately identified.

Cash-flow classification is the central issue. FY26 main-statement CFO₹19.7166 cr differs from the report's MD&A and revised exchange-results CFO₹17.1669 cr by₹2.5497 cr. The offset is financing lease payments, with total cash movement unchanged at−₹20.8351 cr. The newer lease note supports₹4.9049 cr cash lease payments rather than₹2.3552 cr. This offsetting reclassification alone is not grounds to call cash false. More materially, the statements include current borrowing movement in CFO, a large new ROU/lease movement in FY25, and acquired liabilities/provisions in FY26. Those components cannot be equated to customer collections.

The scoped ratio-of-sums is retained rather than hidden. FY22–24 standalone reported CFO₹1.8950 cr divided by PAT₹13.6238 cr is 0.1391 x. Reclassifying only current borrowing gives₹2.8557 cr and 0.2096 x, still not a full normalized cash restatement. FY25–26 consolidated reported CFO₹39.9207 cr divided by PAT₹29.9983 cr is 1.3308 x, but only two years and materially contaminated by the identified lease/acquisition classifications. These perimeters are not pooled into one five-year ratio. FY24 receivable/contract-asset presentation in restated versus later comparable statements also prevents assuming a seamless working-capital series without a mapping.

The acquisition bridge is incomplete in a specific way. Singapore's disclosed US$350 consideration, approximately₹0.0029 cr, is not the₹18.9602 cr goodwill recognized against negative net assets. The₹2.2715 cr consolidated-minus-standalone closing cash difference is not proven cash at the January 8 acquisition date. For Estel, noncontingent consideration totals₹29.32 cr and maximum contingent consideration₹12 cr, with₹10 cr booked. June capital creditors₹7.288 cr may include acquisition and other capital items; the entire balance cannot be asserted to equal unpaid sellers. Therefore exact historical paid consideration and acquisition-date cash remain ND. The future model begins with June cash and pays remaining recorded obligations, rather than deducting the entire acquisition or goodwill a second time.

FY26 CFO includes₹0.3835 cr current borrowing movement; a₹7.9768 cr current-financial-liability increase includes₹7.3633 cr capital-creditor and₹0.6135 cr current-lease movements. Provision increases₹15.6722 cr include₹10 cr performance consideration and₹1.6592 cr acquired employee benefits. These are disclosed components for reconciliation, not a list to subtract blindly: acquired working capital, FX and other noncash movements must be matched on both sides. Similarly, FY25 gross investing additions include₹28.2046 cr new ROU assets; neither that whole amount nor goodwill is recurring cash capex.

The latest quarter gives a narrower cash test. Reported CFO₹3.3736 cr contains₹2 cr current borrowing. Debt-only CFO₹1.3736 cr less₹0.1283 cr capex, ₹1.1609 cr lease cash and₹0.2932 cr nonlease interest leaves−₹0.2088 cr, before debt principal. This is not a fully normalized TTM cash measure, but it prevents calling the quarter strongly self-funding merely from positive statutory CFO.

Working capital corroborates the concern. Billed receivables plus contract assets rose from₹19.8608 cr to₹48.2096 cr, roughly 142.7%, and closing combined days from about 84.5 to 127.3. Prepayments rose to₹10.0107 cr. Billed ageing shows no balances over one year, but unbilled ageing is not supplied, so that statement cannot be extended to all contract assets. Management explains roughly₹6 cr awaiting approvals in two customers and cites past collections; subsequent receipt remains unverified. Goodwill plus IP totals₹68.9465 cr atMarch 2026, about two-thirds of equity, and₹68.9768 cr or 62.78% atJune. Gratuity/leave obligations and nearly absent funding assets are retained as real future claims, not erased by an EBITDA presentation.

A minor source arithmetic exception is also retained: FY22 restated PBT less all printed tax lines gives PAT₹3.5766 cr, while the printed PAT is₹3.5703 cr. The₹0.0063 cr difference equals the prior-tax credit line. Printed PAT is preserved, not silently altered; this small item does not independently drive G2. FY24 original trade receivables₹21.7687 cr equal the later comparative split of₹15.4218 cr billed plus₹6.3469 cr contract assets, so that regrouping is not misread as collection.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The verified issued-share market capitalization is₹416.4778 cr. FY26 reported P/E is 23.0037 x and TTM P/E 20.8518 x, using the same current issued denominator, not a weighted-average EPS denominator for one calculation and diluted shares for another. FY26 sales multiple is 3.0129 x. With June debt₹13.8417 cr and only bank-current/cash₹8.1658 cr netted, rent-basis EV is₹422.1537 cr; including all deposits reduces it to₹413.6529 cr. A lease-inclusive diagnostic EV is₹450.0964 cr. These conventions are labeled and never mixed within the valuation model.

The main model uses cash rent in operating profit and cash flow, so it does not subtract lease debt or lease principal again. Purchased-IP economic amortization is deducted in earnings and added back only as noncash amortization in cash flow, with actual replacement/growth capex retained. Internal development remains an expense. Remaining employee-benefit obligations, seller creditors, performance consideration, debt and an operating reserve are deducted or paid exactly once. There is no extra value for premises already supporting the operating earnings.

All paths start from published June cash and obligations, bridge to the October entry, and stop cash/funding atOctober 20,2031. Cash reserve₹3 cr is an analyst choice, with 0/1.5/3/6 sensitivities, not a legal covenant or observed cash deficit. Base initial available cash is₹8.1658 cr; excluding₹8.5008 cr deposits is conservative because a precise restricted amount is not provided. A separate all-deposits-available case preserves the counterevidence. Legacy current tax₹0.843 cr and statutory dues₹2.4155 cr are scheduled separately, with the latter March balance carried forward as an estimate because June composition is not disclosed. The opening working-capital bridge also labels its March interest/statutory anchors.

Base FY27 CVM revenue grows 18%, while Estel is₹29 cr for a full year, anchored to the nine-month FY26 run rate rather than blindly annualizing Q 1. Subsequent growth is 18% CVM and 10% Estel. Pre-rent operating margins move from 22% to 26% in CVM and 12% to 18% in Estel, with continuing product spending. Base billed/unbilled days are 85/60, other operating assets 7% of revenue, customer advances 4% and payables 1%. Capex is 2.8% of revenue, tax 20%, nonlease borrowing cost 10%, and cash rent starts₹5.2 cr with 5% growth. Capital creditors are paidMarch 2027, booked contingent consideration inMarch 2028/29, and debt principal is modeled at₹2.5 cr annually. Payment dates are assumptions where not disclosed; all opening liabilities and remaining balances are visible.

Bear assumptions are 8%/2% segment growth, weaker margins,115/90 billed/unbilled days,4% capex, maximum₹12 cr contingent consideration, a 15% receivable/contract-asset collection haircut and 10 x terminal EBIT. Bull assumptions use 25%/18% growth, stronger margins,70/40 days,2.5% capex and 20 x EBIT. Base terminal multiple is 16 x normalized rent-basis EBIT. These are analyst ranges, not borrowed peer targets or management promises. The terminal earnings measure is an annualized FY32 run rate while cash only runs to the actual October date; there is no post-horizon cash leakage.

Primary bear and base paths breach the reserve and therefore have no conditional IRR or hurdle entry price. The bear has a pre-entry modeled breach; a later recovery cannot erase it. Funded alternatives include accessible deposits, better operating outcomes, an explicit future-equity rescue and proposed warrants only as a counterfactual. The revised warrant proposal is 685,000 shares at₹400, not the superseded 700,000 proposal. Its approval vote onOctober 21 is outside the cutoff. The counterfactual receives 25% inNovember 2026 and 75% inMay 2028, tests cash immediately before receipt, and adds shares on exercise. These amounts are not current liquidity.

Rescue pre-funds each interval using whole shares at 75% of the candidate entry price, with 3% issuance costs. Gross money, fees, net money, share expansion and the original owners' lost ownership fraction reconcile separately. Entry-price hurdles re-run the model at each candidate price so dilution is self-consistent; simply discounting terminal value calculated at₹393 would be wrong. Granted₹295 options exercise at exit only when economically in the money, with exercise proceeds and shares together. They are not forced into the bear case as convenient cash.

The fifty two-way stresses combine collection days with exit multiples, reserve with capex, and accessible deposits with contingent consideration. Six reverse solvers find funded bracket crossings and verify residuals for 12/15/18% target returns, solving both required CVM growth and exit multiple under explicit rescue. The full model and annual rows are embedded. None of these conditional outputs overrides the unresolved G2 gate or becomes an ordinary expected return, buy price or price-implied score.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A permanent-loss path does not require the product to fail completely. Operator launches can remain commercially relevant while approval delays keep recognized revenue unbilled, billed receivables grow, staff and hosting costs require cash, and acquisition payments fall due. A collection haircut can then coincide with slower new wins and lower margins. Accounting goodwill provides no readily realizable cash buffer for those obligations.

The bear model combines weaker growth, longer billed/unbilled cycles, higher maintenance/growth capex, the maximum contingent payment and a lower terminal multiple. Without new financing it breaches the selected reserve before entry and has no valid return estimate. This is a deliberately adverse counterfactual, not a statement that the company actually lacked cash inAugust 2026. Published deposits and actual collections could materially change that historical bridge.

The explicit bear rescue illustrates the economic cost if equity is available at a discount. Large additional funds and share issuance protect the modeled cash floor but dilute the old holders; optional₹295 employee shares are not exercised when out of the money. The resulting negative annualized ownership return is a conditional permanent-loss illustration, not a probability-weighted forecast. If investors refuse rescue capital, operational disruption or creditor enforcement could be worse than this smoothly financed path.

There are important offsets. June total cash exceeds reported financial debt; current auditors report no actual debt default; internal development is expensed; many revenues arise from ongoing operator relationships. G3 therefore remains Conditional rather than Fail. D 4 captures a meaningful loss path with tangible counterevidence, while G2 remains the distinct accounting-reliability hurdle. A lower share price alone cannot fix poor collections, and a high terminal multiple cannot finance an earlier cash trough.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome over the exact horizon requires 37.95% annualized owner return; tenfold requires 58.45%. Business revenue growth and shareholder return are not interchangeable because dilution, margins, financing, cash and the exit multiple intervene. The test uses the explicitly rescued base path's terminal shares, including in-the-money options, rather than pretending today's share count is permanent.

At that denominator, fivefold implies roughly₹2,190.32 cr equity value and tenfold₹4,380.64 cr. With the modeled terminal net-cash/obligation bridge and 16 x normalized EBIT, required EBIT isabout₹131.82 cr and₹268.71 cr respectively. At an illustrative 20% post-rent, post-IP EBIT margin, required revenue isabout₹659.10 cr and₹1,343.57 cr. Relative to₹151.7589 cr TTM revenue, the corresponding revenue growth rates are 34.12% and 54.64% over the same exact horizon. These are algebraic feasibility conditions, not forecasts.

The fivefold case needs sustained high growth, cross-selling and new operator wins, materially better cash realization, and no large unmodeled dilution. The tenfold case is substantially more demanding and cannot be justified by calling the company a tiny fraction of management's TAM. The market-share denominator is not independently validated, and reachable customer wallet differs from total industry opportunity. Neither scenario receives a numerical probability or a high-quality-compounder label. Better collection economics could make the business more valuable even without a fivefold share-price outcome.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First priority is a signed cash-to-cash reconciliation, not another revenue headline. Request a FY24–26 bridge separating acquired cash and acquired working capital, paid versus unpaid consideration, lease recognition versus payment, borrowing movements, FX, provisions and operating collections. Reconcile the FY25 comparative regrouping and FY26 lease classification without assuming the offsetting items are fraud. Successful reconciliation can clear G2 even if historical conversion remains weak; failure to explain material movements sustains the hold.

Track contract assets through opening balance, recognized revenue, invoice issuance, actual receipts, write-offs and closing balance by ageing bucket. The roughly₹6 cr awaiting approval should be followed to dated acceptance and bank realization, not merely management reassurance. Monitor combined billed/unbilled days, prepayments and customer advances together, so moving an amount between labels does not look like collection improvement. A practical improvement signal is two consecutive half-years of positive normalized cash after product upkeep, rent and nonlease interest without fresh borrowing masking it.

For liquidity, establish how much of₹8.5008 cr deposits is available, exact seller-creditor obligations, contingent-payment triggers and dates, employee-benefit payments, debt maturities and committed undrawn facilities. The conservative base reserve gap isabout₹4.27 cr; accessible resources or demonstrable incremental collections can close it without assuming a placement. Re-run reserve, capex and collection sensitivities whenever a new result arrives. Treat October 21 warrant voting, any later allotment and actual cash receipts as new dated events, never as cutoff facts.

For earnings and execution, compare CVM/Estel growth, margins and incremental employee cost; separate one-time licenses, change requests and contracted recurring amounts where possible. Track acquired-IP useful life, R&D expense, tax normalization and dilution-adjusted EPS. Preserve management guidance dates and measurement definitions before judging promises. Follow the former-UK-shareholder claim, pledge changes, related-party balances and control exceptions with both adverse and favorable evidence.

For implementation, refresh the official series/lot, complete the missing sessions, and inspect current depth, spreads, circuits and applicable restrictions for the real order size. sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: research hold, speculative growth watchlist. Pelatro is a real product-led telecom software business with encouraging acquisition-adjusted revenue growth and potentially attractive asset-light operating leverage. It is not currently established as a high-quality cash-compounding investment under this framework.

The decisive issue is not that software development is capitalized: internal development is expensed. It is that a changing legal perimeter, purchased capabilities, lease/noncash accounting, working-capital expansion and deferred obligations prevent a trustworthy normalized operating-cash and incremental-capital bridge. Clean recent audit opinions, published liquidity and management explanations are retained as counterevidence, not ignored to force a negative verdict.

No ordinary entry price, expected return, target price or position recommendation is issued while G2 is held. All three aggregate scores are NS and excluded from rankings. Conditional funded-case prices and returns are analytical illustrations only. The appropriate next action is to resolve the identified reconciliation and funding questions, update the model from the next authenticated results and actual fundraising/collection events, and reassess. A lower quotation is not itself clearance, and a later warrant approval does not retroactively supply cash at the research cutoff.

This is general company research, not personalized financial advice. The illustrative₹500,000 order and 15% hurdle are methodological assumptions; suitability depends on the investor's circumstances, concentration and ability to tolerate SME liquidity and permanent loss.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence includes full original annual financial reports, restated and pro forma IPO financial statements, the SEBI prospectus, quarterly exchange results and clarification, annual audit/CARO/control annexures, management calls, issuer corporate-action documents, shareholding patterns, monitoring reports, the SEBI order and dated NSE market/security files. The source register retains URLs, retrieval dates, document date precision and original-byte hashes. Company statements, allegations, analyst inferences, calculated facts and forward assumptions are distinguished.

The full record embeds all annual/interim financial rows, TTM arithmetic, cash and capital bridges, factor/evidence records, all seven scenario forecasts, monthly funding paths, fifty sensitivities with annual rows, reverse solvers and multibagger algebra. Unavailable fields remain null/ND rather than zero. Numerical estimates use explicit units and deterministic Decimal calculations; displayed rounding does not alter underlying values. Mathematical reproduction is not independent authentication of the source documents or a guarantee that assumptions will occur.

Key open questions are exact acquisition cash paid and acquired cash at each transfer date; seller-creditor attribution and maturity; the full operating/financing/noncash bridge; amount and terms of encumbered deposits; contract-asset ageing and later collections; audited recurring/license/services mix; retention/pricing/cohort returns; stable organic invested-capital attribution; FY26 customer concentration; future tax/IP-life economics; and current executable market depth/restrictions. The lack of private daily bank statements alone does not justify declaring the company unfinanceable.

Forward assumptions include growth and margin paths, working-capital days,20% tax,10% borrowing cost, purchased-IP ten-year economic life, cash-rent growth, capex/reserve policy, legacy dues timing, seller/contingent payments, benefit accruals and optional financing terms. The ₹1 final dividend was approved at the August 3 AGM; August 31 is an assumed pre-entry payment date, not a verified transfer date. The October 21 warrant vote and all later events are excluded from factual cutoff conclusions. Both favorable and adverse scenarios are shown, but no unsupported probability-weighted return is manufactured.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Historical compliance breaches and unresolved minority allegations require monitoring, but current records do not establish material Pelatro diversion or manipulation. The company response and clean later control reports are retained.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: Material operating-cash reliance is central to the thesis, yet financing movements, acquired liabilities and noncash lease/goodwill components are not reconciled into a credible recurring cash measure. The FY26 lease reclassification and unchanged cash/PAT are not separately called fraud or profit errors.
gates.clearance: Issuer/auditor-supported FY24–26 cash-to-cash acquisition/lease/borrowing bridge and explicit comparative regrouping explanation. Closing cash may be reliable while operating classification remains unsuitable for valuation.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Published June cash plus accessible deposits could support the base case; the conservative bank-current-only case needs approximately₹4.27cr additional available resources/collections to retain a₹3cr reserve. No observed default or actual October cash deficit is claimed. Optional warrants cannot be treated received.
gates.clearance: Establish available deposit/committed-line quantum and remaining seller payment dates; re-run linked stress. This is not a demand for private daily bank statements.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.reason: Dated exchange row verifies trading and lot300, but only58/60 observations, thin lot-capacity and unverified live spread/circuit/depth prevent an implementation clearance. It is not a suspension finding.
gates.clearance: Authenticate missing sessions/restrictions and actual-size order-book capacity.

GOV.rationale: Promoter ownership aligns incentives, and recent audit reports are clean. Historical compliance penalties, an unresolved minority-shareholder allegation and complex cash presentation justify caution, not a fraud conclusion.
GOV.what_changes_it: Resolve the UK claim with dated documents, reconcile transaction consideration, and sustain clear control reporting.

MOAT.rationale: Operator integration, embedded data and long deployments create switching friction. Retention, pricing and cohort-return evidence are insufficient to demonstrate exceptional structural economics; broad platforms and internal teams compete.
MOAT.what_changes_it: Disclose renewals, churn, net retention, customer returns and pricing alongside collected gross-profit cohorts.

REV.rationale: The explicit two-year constant-perimeter exception uses FY24 pro forma CVM revenue of ₹73.0274cr and FY26 ₹116.5686cr, giving 26.3420% CAGR and the schedule score of 8. FY26 core growth of 35.91% and Q1 core growth of 25.11% support direction, without a quarterly bonus. A five- or three-year comparable group organic series is unavailable.
REV.what_changes_it: Add a three- or five-year constant-scope audited series and currency, price and volume bridge.

DUR.rationale: Cross-selling CVM products and Estel distribution/digital-finance tools is an accessible adjacency within existing operators. Long sales cycles, collection friction, a finite operator universe and AI competition limit certainty.
DUR.what_changes_it: Demonstrate paid deployments, cohort expansion and renewals on normal collection terms.

CAP.rationale: Expensed development and modest physical capital needs can support attractive software economics. Acquisitions, purchased IP, a new lease and noncash consolidation movements prevent a matched organic incremental NOPAT/invested-capital estimate. Current ROCE is not a substitute, and unknown is not low return.
CAP.what_changes_it: Provide a complete cash/noncash acquisition and organic capital bridge with matched profit maturation; useful aggregate evidence can suffice without private project cohorts.

CASH.rationale: Weak realization is supported by three-year standalone conversion, management cash-shortfall commentary, rising unbilled/prepaid balances and negative Q1 debt-adjusted cash after capex, rent and other interest. Reported group CFO contains identified financing and noncash components.
CASH.what_changes_it: Reconcile group conversion, show dated unbilled invoicing and collections, and establish two halves of positive self-funded cash generation.

BAL.rationale: Published June total cash could fund the base case if enough deposits are accessible. The bank-current-only case breaches a chosen reserve. Debt is moderate, but lease rent, seller creditors, contingent payments and underfunded employee benefits make liquidity important. No actual default is established.
BAL.what_changes_it: Confirm available deposits or committed facilities and seller-payment dates; do not rely on proposed warrants as received money.

EXEC.rationale: Core growth and Estel revenue integration are visible achievements. Q1 Estel margins softened and cash realization lags the intended self-funding transition. Management target coverage is not collected cash or an independently reconciled absolute order book.
EXEC.what_changes_it: Track cash-backed milestones, integration margins and like-for-like target outcomes.

EARN.rationale: Operating profit and per-share earnings improved while internal development is expensed. Material FX/other income, a low effective tax rate, acquisition mix and unamortized purchased IP mean reported PAT is not equivalent to recurring organic owner earnings.
EARN.what_changes_it: Validate normalized taxes, acquired-IP useful life, recurring segment margins and fully diluted EPS.

R.rationale: No ordinary expected-return score is assigned while the material G2 operating-cash reliability issue is unresolved. Funded counterfactual and explicit rescue IRRs are illustrations, not expected-return estimates.
R.what_changes_it: Resolve the cash and financeability basis, then select defensible probabilities for funded scenarios against the 15% hurdle.

D.rationale: Operator concentration, slow collections, intangible-heavy equity and acquisition obligations create a credible permanent-loss path. Recurring software relationships and published liquidity provide counterweight; stress loss is not an observed-default claim.
D.what_changes_it: Improve collected cash, verify liquid-resource access and reduce obligations without destructive dilution.

P.rationale: Reverse expectations are calculated only under explicitly funded or rescued assumptions. Without a reliable cash normalization and funding basis, classifying current expectations as easy or heroic would be unsupported.
P.what_changes_it: Establish cash funding and normalized earnings before scoring price-implied growth and margins.

L.rationale: The official dated price, lot and 58 observed sessions support useful diagnostics, but two missing rows are not zero. Live depth, spread and point-in-time restrictions are not sufficiently authenticated for a complete implementation score.
L.what_changes_it: Fill missing dates, verify restrictions and depth, and recalculate for the actual intended position.

GQS.cap_reason: Persistent weak cash realization triggers the framework maximum of 5. The uncapped missing-data range is retained separately, the upper policy ceiling is 5, and the unavailable point score remains NS.

ranking_exclusion_reason: Material G2 hold and unavailable composite points; conditional models do not cure missing factors.

summary:
Pelatro has a credible software growth proposition, but its operating-cash presentation and acquisition bridge are not yet reliable enough for an ordinary investment rating. Classification: research hold, with a speculative growth watchlist rather than a confirmed compounder designation. This is not a short recommendation or a finding of fraud.

The positive case is substantial. FY26 CVM revenue rose 35.91% without counting Estel's acquired revenue, and the next quarter's core growth was 25.11%. Internal product development is expensed, a favorable feature often missed when all software intangibles are called capitalized R&D. Telecom integrations and cross-selling can produce useful operating leverage. At the verified ₹393 reference price, reported TTM P/E is 20.85 x rather than an obviously prohibitive multiple.

The obstacle is the distinction between profit, growth and money available to owners. Receivables plus unbilled assets grew about 142.7%, to ₹48.21 cr, against 61.2% reported sales growth. Prepayments also expanded sharply. The published cash-flow statements contain borrowing, acquired-liability and noncash lease/goodwill movements that prevent a clean normalized conversion measure. Existing audits are unmodified, but that does not make every operating-cash classification suitable for valuation.

BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, without neutral imputation. Individual strengths and weaknesses are scored where evidence supports them. A base case excluding deposits needs additional accessible cash or collections to maintain the analyst's reserve; using all published deposits keeps it funded. Therefore G3 is Conditional, not an actual-distress finding. Until the G2 reconciliation is resolved, attractive conditional model returns must not be promoted as an expected return or executable buy price.
